response: Yes, juvenile osteochondritis dissecans (JOCD) is suggested to be associated with a growth disturbance of the secondary physis of the epiphysis. MRI studies of children with OCD have consistently shown secondary physis disruption, overlying chondroepiphysial widening, and subchondral bone edema, indicating that disruption of normal endochondral ossification may be involved in the development of JOCD. This implies that JOCD can be considered a growth disturbance of the secondary physis of the epiphysis.
